record.file_problem: The full paper and appendix are present. The text has some PDF extraction/flattening artifacts in tables, but the relevant results are mostly interpretable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether models can be aligned and fused using a layer-wise optimal-transport mapping, reporting fused-model performance. This is a different method and outcome from the original sources, and bears most directly on V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many model-fusion results that bear on whether mapped models can be combined while retaining performance. Its ResNet layerwise OT-cost plot (Figure S3) is described as an example for inspecting representation similarity, but the text gives no interpretable outcome from that plot; the paper also says an extensive study is beyond its scope. Accuracy results about pruning, teacher-student transfer, and distillation are not included unless they directly test the mapped-representation claim.
record.test_reason: The paper aligns neurons of separately trained same-architecture networks with OT (exact OT gives a permutation, a linear map) and reports one-shot accuracy of the averaged model. That accuracy loss is an indirect measure of how well one network's units map onto another's, so it bears on V4. This is a different method from either original source. Finetuned results mostly reflect retraining, not mapping quality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that OT-based layerwise neuron alignment before weight averaging is a versatile fusion tool. It enables one-shot knowledge transfer without sharing data, significantly outperforms vanilla averaging in all settings, and allows fusing different-width models (pruning, compression). With finetuning, the fused model can replace an ensemble. They concede that one-shot fusion of seed-only CIFAR models does not beat the individual models, attributing this to the greedy layerwise alignment, and that the width-dependent gap shrinks as width grows.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses layer-wise OT matching and parameter averaging to fuse models; it is not a reproduction of either original source's representation-similarity method.
record.method_sensitivity: Fusion accuracy changes with activation mini-batch size and Sinkhorn regularization; exact OT generally performs better than regularized OT. The paper also reports different results for activation- versus weight-based alignment and says multiple iterations can improve ResNet fusion.

fits_no_version.finding: OT-fused models, after finetuning, match or slightly exceed parent accuracy while vanilla averages fail to retrain with 4+ models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Permutation/OT alignment makes weight-space averaging of differently seeded networks a usable starting point for retraining (model-fusion utility).

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2020 (34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, as stated in the paper)
record.problems: Most reported outcomes are task accuracy after weight fusion, an indirect measure of representation interchangeability. The paper's similarity-focused ResNet layerwise OT-cost result is only shown as a figure and is not interpreted numerically in the text. The layerwise procedure is described as greedy; one-shot results can be substantially below parent-model performance. Some reported uncertainty is limited to selected experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted repeated detailed finetuning sweeps and the same headline results reprinted in Appendix S3 and S9; the kept rows capture the separately stated headline conditions. Omitted model-pruning and teacher-student results because they do not directly test the claim's mapping of independently trained representations. Omitted Figure S3's layerwise ResNet18 OT costs because the text provides no interpretable numerical outcomes.

untested.parts: No comparison across architectures, objectives or data with scale or capability.
No direct measure of shared features or subspaces across seeds. Vanilla-averaging failure plus OT success is only indirectly consistent with it.
No linear regression maps, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment. No cross-architecture mapping beyond width differences within one architecture family.
Sensitivity is to fusion settings, not to a representation-similarity metric.

missing.what: One-shot skill-transfer fusion of MLPNets trained on heterogeneous data with different initializations: OT 93.11 vs parents 89.78/87.35; plus a 4-model same-init case at 93.6%.
One-shot OT fusion across different widths (teacher into student): MLPNet 95.67/96.50 vs MB 97.84/97.08; VGG11 86.73/88.40 vs MB 90.66/89.38.
missing.locator: Table S12 (OT avg. column); Section 5.2 Figure 4

missing.what: Output-layer transport map has trace/sum ≈1, showing alignment recovers the known identical ordering.
Same- vs different-initialization comparison: vanilla averaging works much better with shared init, showing unit ordering differs across seeds.

record.verdict_notes: Multiple value errors: r5 and r7 copied finetuned values, r26, r27 and r29 confused the OT-average and MA-aligned columns, and r19–r24 took the MA-aligned column as the vanilla baseline. Fused accuracy is an indirect proxy for representational interchangeability. The width trend (gap falls from 14.44% to 0.86%) is a within-architecture size effect on alignability, not V1.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether alignment between independently trained models with differing architectures, objectives, data, or modalities rises with scale and capability.
No paired image-caption or vision-language comparison.

Models trained from different initializations are fused, but the paper does not test whether they learn many of the same features or shared subspaces. It mentions layerwise OT costs as a possible similarity-inspection tool, without a textual result establishing convergence.
Tests OT-based neuron/weight alignment and parameter averaging on image-classification models; does not test linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits.

The paper compares alignment settings and reports their effects on fusion accuracy, but does not test whether measured representation convergence itself depends on similarity measure, neighbour count, or input distribution.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain convergence, or whether cross-model representation alignment plateaus.
